editorial.headline: Independent Medical Practice: Open Nationally, Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Independent general care and treatment by doctors is open nationally to 100% foreign ownership, but the activity is closed to PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
This activity is the independent provision of general care and treatment for illness by doctors. Its scope is deliberately narrow in its wording: it concerns services for general illness, performed independently by a doctor. That makes the independence of the practitioner central to the activity, alongside the actual provision of care and treatment. For a founder, the useful reading is not merely health services, but an independent doctor’s practice whose work is general care and treatment of disease.

Registration is open at every scale named in the record: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. This is a meaningful part of the classification: it places the activity across the full stated scale range instead of confining it to a single business size. The scale field, however, should be read for what it says. It confirms availability at those four scales; it does not by itself alter the defining premise that the service is independently provided by a doctor.

At the national level, the PMA status is open and the maximum foreign ownership is 100%. In plain terms, the national record permits full foreign ownership of this activity. Bali changes the result completely. Its Bali status is closed, and the record marks PMA registration as blocked. The honest conclusion for a foreign founder is direct: an independent doctor’s practice under this activity cannot be registered in Bali today. The recorded reason is a Health Ministry health-law restriction: a foreign doctor cannot open a solo practice. This is the stated substantive barrier, rather than a minor administrative qualification.

The Bali record also contains a province-wide, permanent PMA rule: it blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities across the island. It is sourced to Governor’s letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. That provincial rule sits beside the activity’s explicit Bali closure and the stated restriction on a foreign doctor’s solo practice. National openness should therefore be read as the national position only; it does not turn Bali’s closed PMA registration status into an available route.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness does not turn Bali’s closed PMA registration status into an available route.
